about.title: Eastvale Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a crash on I-15, Schleisman Road, or another Eastvale corridor takes a life, the people left behind face more than sorrow. There are funeral arrangements, missing income, and a household that now has to adjust to a loss no one planned for. California law gives certain family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim against the party responsible. Riverside County families in Eastvale often want to understand this process quickly, since the deadline to act is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter if a government entity is involved. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect grieving families with an independent attorney who can explain standing, evaluate the claim, and handle the legal work while you focus on your family. There's no upfront cost, and the attorney only gets paid if there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Eastvale Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, and children, then other dependents or heirs. An independent attorney can clarify where your family fits before any claim moves forward.

items.title: Racing Against a Real Deadline
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file, but that window shrinks significantly if a government entity is involved, which matters on roads like I-15. Getting matched with an attorney early helps protect that timeline.

items.title: Recovering What the Law Allows
items.desc: California recognizes losses like funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney in our network can help identify which of these apply to your family's circumstances.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation to confirm who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Eastvale?
items.answer: California law typically allows two years from the date of death, though that period is shorter when a government agency, such as one responsible for road maintenance on a corridor like Limonite Avenue, may be involved. Because these deadlines are strict, it helps to speak with an attorney as soon as your family is ready.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No, they're separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action seeking compensation for the family's losses. One can proceed regardless of the outcome of the other.
